## Moments and vanishing

**Topic scope:** Generalized vanishing, Gaussian moments and Image/Mathieu spaces.

**Computed obligation progress:** 6 open.

The universal GVC/GMC dimension classifications and Gaussian dimension-degree boundary are claimed closed in their exact domains. Higher-dimensional GMC is refuted by witnesses; general Gaussian extensions is not an unrestricted open GMC claim.

Safety-to-purity is the converse implication to GMC. Its primitive-vacuum equivalence is represented in one direction with equivalence metadata to preserve acyclicity.

Two-base marker generation supplies a proved reduction, while purity-to-base-marker polynomiality and complete bidegree-(3,3) Image coverage remain mathematical gaps.

Two-pair bidegree-(3,3) now has an exact sixteen-parameter sphere model, complete even parity coverage, odd parity coverage dependent on the internal Gaussian classification, and exact seven- and ten-parameter mixed-slice certificates. Purity-to-frame extraction and the full thirteen-parameter affine sphere family remain open; the least failing balanced degree is still three or four.

### GAUSSIAN-H21-AFFINE-CHART

[Gaussian H(2,1): affine charts, radial phases and obstructions](moments/vanishing/GAUSSIAN_AFFINE_ISOTROPIC_CHART.md)

**Exact scope:** Complete all-degree purity classification for Wh(Z)+v(Z)Y^2+b(Z)Y+k(Z), with explicit safe marker cutoffs and no nonisotropic constant-fibre axis for its unsafe branch. For B=c(Z)W+u(Z), g=Wh(Z)+k(Z), all pure members are safe if deg c<=2, with unrestricted h,u,k. More generally, for nonconstant c whose root multiplicities are at most two, purity is equivalent to a=0, h,c divisible by Z^2, u,k divisible by Z. Thus nonconstant squarefree c of arbitrary degree has no pure members. For arbitrary multiplicities nonconstant c excludes purity when a!=0; unshared roots of c,h also have no multiplicity restriction. For a nonzero constant lambda, every pure phase lambda W^2+Wh(Z)+c(Z)WY+aY^2+u(Z)Y+k(Z) is quadratic; nonconstant c(Z) admits no pure member, by a connected double-cover period argument retaining positive-genus cycles. Every all-degree radial phase aY^2+B(ZW)Y+g(ZW) is pure only if it is zero, using a relative endpoint module of rank D and a complete endpoint period pairing. Consequently weakly one-sided angular support is safe in all degrees, with cutoff m>deg Q. A fixed-multipuncture logarithmic seed estimate and an ordinary-volume estimate at double roots supply these extensions, using the stated comparison dependencies. No polynomial automorphism preserving 2ZW+Y^2 sends Long's quartic into H(2,1). General H(2,1) remains open.

**Authored state:** proved. **Graph state:** proved. **Dependency coverage:** partial.

**Recorded assurances:** Independent replay: not recorded; Formal verification: not recorded; External review: not recorded.

**Current blockers:** none in declared routes.

**Verification limits:** Internal source reviews checked the multipuncture completeness/tail argument, exact Puiseux-disc charts, double-root generic/neck valuations, arbitrary-multiplicity nonzero-a obstruction, rank-D relative endpoint pairing, spatial half-density elimination and connected double-cover component estimates, retaining positive-genus cycles. The current comparison-source revisions were inspected and do not change the used hypotheses. Semistable reduction and nodal resolution primary statements and their justifications were inspected. Exact symbolic identities and bounded Wick controls passed on current bytes. These controls do not prove the all-degree results or the imported comparison theorems. Independent mathematical review, formal verification and external review remain pending.

**Topic scope:** Polynomial Keller maps, their fibres, monodromy and boundary geometry.

Retained ordinary characteristic-zero polynomial Keller constructions have determinant one and explicit collisions; their internal consequence is failure of the unrestricted Jacobian conjecture. JC2 remains a separate unresolved target. Ruling degree, generic map degree, graph degree and sparse support minima are distinct quantities.

## Hessian and Schur reductions

**Topic scope:** Restricted Hessian classes, polynomial graphs and formal termination.

**Computed obligation progress:** 4 open.

The degree-five graph exclusion concerns a fixed v2 parent and graph degree, not all potentials or embeddings.

Ricci-flat HC4 is a restricted sufficient theorem using the attributed Tang structural alternative. Scalar curvature does not substitute for Ricci flatness. Retained invertible cotangent examples have nonzero Ricci, so Ricci flatness is not necessary for invertibility.

## Formal verification

**Topic scope:** Precisely scoped Lean developments supporting published papers and current manuscripts.

**Computed obligation progress:** 6 open.

Formal verification is scoped by exact declarations, transitive assumptions and the paper bridge. A paper theorem does not imply that its full formalization is complete.

GMC2 retains two explicit mathematical axiom interfaces, shown as open formalization obligations. Its propagated formal claim remains conditional until discharged; its written mathematical theorem has separate proof support.

Binary GVC and generic tangent-pencil geometry are partial formalizations. The focused finite-etale certificate excludes the broader supplied-presentation and analytic counting scopes. No Lean build was rerun for this registry migration.
